title: Complete Relational Description of Spin in a Quantum Background
authors: Hannah Troger, Ofek Bengyat, Thomas D. Galley, Marios Christodoulou
abstract: The standard description of the state of a spin in quantum mechanics presupposes externally fixed directions -- a classical background. Can a spin be fully described instead in relation to other quantum mechanical systems? Poulin suggested twenty years ago group averaging over rotations the joint state of a fundamental spin and a reference spin with large angular momentum which, however, yields a classical bit in a probabilistic mixture. We revisit this idea and show that when the quantum reference system is augmented to \emph{two} large spins, the standard quantum mechanical description of a spin is recovered in the limit of large quantum numbers for the reference system.
summary: The paper tackles the challenge of describing quantum spin without relying on an external classical reference frame. By coupling the target spin to two large auxiliary spins and employing group averaging techniques, the authors demonstrate that a complete, coherent description of the qubit state can be recovered in the appropriate large-limit regime.
main_problem: The central problem is developing a description of quantum spin that is fully relational, meaning its state is independent of an externally fixed classical background reference frame.
main_result: Using two large, orthogonal reference spins allows the relational encoding procedure to successfully recover the full coherence of the original pure qubit state in the limit of large reference angular momenta.
method: The authors employ group averaging techniques (both coherent and incoherent) on the joint density matrix of the target spin and the composite reference system over $SO(3)$ rotations.
model_or_system: The model involves a fundamental spin-1/2 system ($S$) coupled to two large quantum reference spins ($G$ and $H$). The analysis is performed using recoupling theory and group representation methods.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing the results from coherent versus incoherent group averaging, with the conclusion favoring the coherent average for background independence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition: a single reference spin yields only classical mixtures, while adding a second spin restores coherence. Other figures show convergence of probability distributions to specific asymptotic limits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the failure of a single reference spin (Poulin's idea), then introducing and calculating the result for two spins ($G$ and $H$), followed by a detailed comparison between coherent and incoherent averaging methods, and concluding with general statements on ideal encoding.
why_interesting: This work addresses fundamental issues in quantum gravity and background independence by providing a concrete mathematical framework to define physical observables (like spin) purely relative to other quantum systems, which is crucial for theories where spacetime itself is quantized.
